correctness.rationale: An A proposal at time u is accepted iff independently shielded from B on both exterior sides, yielding P(A)=alpha integral h_A^2 with h_A prime=-beta h_B and h_B prime=-alpha h_A. For A endpoints at times u,v two apart, the only central obstruction is a B proposal before min(u,v), producing the exact factor 1-beta min(u,v). Integrating gives alpha^2(H_A^2-beta M_A). Strict h_A(s)^2<1-beta s holds for 0<s<=1 because f(s)=h_A(s)^2+beta s is strictly convex, f(0)=1 and f(1)<1, checked through alpha(1+beta/2)^2<1. This makes the covariance integrand positive. Standard-library finite rational checker independently gives 8,859 passed finite and numerical assertions; these are not used as an infinite-volume proof. Decreasing-time ancestor chains control the infinite limit.

value.rationale: The first nonconsecutive two-site law is a natural structural statistic of accepted cluster separation, measuring interactions not determined by one-site coverage or contiguous monochromatic block densities. The unexpected uniform sign, valid for every time and nontrivial bias, provides a mathematically motivated boundary for spatial correlations in one-shot antagonistic adsorption, and the separated A-X-A probability is directly usable as a two-cluster gap frequency.
